_source:
Curriculum Development Centre Teaching Module — "Fashion and Fabrics Teaching Module Form 1 - Term 2" (https://library.cdcrepository.info/resource.php?id=310). Topic/sub-topic structure and competencies extracted with AI assistance (Gemini) directly from this module's own stated content — never invented; the extraction was instructed to use only what the module itself says, and to flag anything unclear rather than guess. Covers only the term this specific module addresses (Term 2) — other terms are not included since no source document for them was available at extraction time. AI-flagged completeness notes from extraction: 1. Section 1.6 contains minor numbering irregularities in the source text where 'Sub-topic: Yarns' is marked with heading '1.6.1 Sub-topic: Yarns' immediately following '1.6.1 Sub-topic: Fibres', and Specific Competence '1.6.2.1' is listed under it.
2. In Topic 1.7, section 1.7.1 lacks an explicit 'Sub-topic: [Name]' header, jumping directly to 'Specific Competence 1.7.1.1: Create suitable textile design' and 'Activity 1: Explaining the key elements of design'; it was extracted under the descriptive title '1.7.1 Elements of Design' based on the section activity content.
3. Competencies were extracted from both the overarching 'General Competence(s)' blocks and the 'Specific Competence' headings explicit to each section. ADDED (2026-08-28): Term 3 content. Topic/sub-topic structure and competencies extracted with AI assistance (Gemini) directly from this module's own stated content — never invented; the extraction was instructed to use only what the module itself says, and to flag anything unclear rather than guess. Term confirmed directly against the CDC library's own term filter (browse.php?...&term=3), not assumed. AI-flagged completeness notes from extraction: The module text starts mid-sequence at topic number 1.9 ('1.9 TOPIC: GARMENT CONSTRUCTION'), meaning topics 1.1 through 1.8 are missing from this text block. Under Suggested Teaching Methodologies, item 10 is listed with no text. Additionally, detailed sample lesson plans and appendices are appended after the main topics.

subject.name: Fashion and Fabrics
subject.description: Fashion and Fabrics syllabus, Form 1-4 (Curriculum Development Centre).

grade.name: Form 1
grade.phase: Secondary — the source scheme itself uses "Form 1" for this level under the 2023 CBC.

topics.name: TOPIC 1.5: TOOLS AND EQUIPMENT
topics.description: This topic covers various needlework tools and equipment essential for garment construction and household furnishings. It focuses on the usage, selection, care, maintenance, and functions of tools and equipment, including operating the sewing machine.

sub_topics.name: 1.5.1 Sub-topic: Needlework tools
sub_topics.description: Focuses on the use, choice, care, classification, and storage of hand sewing tools such as needles, tape measures, scissors, thimbles, and marking items to achieve precision and safety.

competencies.description: Analytical thinking: Describing the function of needlework tools and equipment
Emotional intelligence: Creating a tool kit with labelled pictures of various needlework tools and equipment
Problem solving: Using needlework tools correctly
Specific Competence: Use of needlework tools

sub_topics.name: 1.5.2 Sub-topic: Needlework Equipment
sub_topics.description: Explores major needlework equipment such as pressing irons, tailor's dummies, full-length mirrors, and chest of drawers, detailing their specific functions and care routines like dusting, covering, and oiling.

competencies.description: Critical thinking: Exploring different needlework equipment
Specific Competence: Use needlework equipment

sub_topics.name: 1.5.3 Sub-topic: The Sewing Machines
sub_topics.description: Covers the types, parts, selection, care, operation, and safety guidelines for sewing machines, guiding learners through setup, bobbin insertion, straight stitching, and basic maintenance.

competencies.description: Problem solving: Operating the sewing machine
Specific competence: Use a sewing machine

topics.name: 1.6 TOPIC: FIBRES AND FABRICS
topics.description: Explores the sources, types, properties, and uses of different natural and synthetic fibres and fabrics, emphasizing their transformation processes and sustainability in everyday life and industry.

sub_topics.name: 1.6.1 Sub-topic: Fibres
sub_topics.description: Examines raw textile units, classifying them into natural and synthetic origins, examining their physical properties, uses, and identification techniques such as burning, microscopic examination, and solubility tests.

competencies.description: Analytical thinking: Differentiate between natural and man-made fibres
Environmental Sustainability: Understand the importance of sustainable practices in fibre and fabric production
Digital Literacy: Use digital tools to research and explore the sources, types, properties, and uses of different fibres and fabrics
Creativity and Innovation: Apply knowledge of fibre properties to select suitable fabrics for specific purposes

sub_topics.name: 1.6.2 Sub-topic: Yarns
sub_topics.description: Focuses on the conversion of raw fibres into continuous strands of yarn through carding, spinning, and plying, analyzing yarn structures (single, ply, fancy) and basic knitting techniques.

competencies.description: Communication: Explain the processes involved in converting fibres into fabrics
Specific Competence: Practice the process of transforming fibres to yarns

sub_topics.name: 1.6.3 Sub-topic: Fabrics
sub_topics.description: Details the methods of converting yarns into fabrics, covering properties like strength, absorbency, and durability, as well as fabric construction via plain, twill, and satin weaves, and weft and warp knits.

competencies.description: Analytical thinking: Identify various types of fabrics and their characteristics
Specific Competence: Practice the process of transforming yarns to fabrics

sub_topics.name: 1.6.4 Sub-topic: Colour Application
sub_topics.description: Explores how colour affects mood, fabric characteristics, and aesthetics, while introducing traditional and modern colouring methods such as dyeing, printing, and painting using natural and synthetic colourants.

competencies.description: Specific Competence: Create desired artworks on Fabrics

sub_topics.name: 1.6.5 Sub-topic: Methods of Colour Application
sub_topics.description: Focuses on colour theory, the colour wheel, color schemes (primary, secondary, complementary, analogous), practical cotton fabric dyeing, and testing for colour fastness.

competencies.description: Specific Competence: Apply colour on fabrics

topics.name: TOPIC 1.7: CLOTHING DESIGN
topics.description: Combines art, culture, and technical principles to conceptualize, sketch, and develop functional, aesthetically pleasing garments suited to personal style, identity, and specific body shapes.

sub_topics.name: 1.7.1 Elements of Design
sub_topics.description: Introduces the basic visual building blocks of garment creation—line, shape, form, colour, texture, space, and value—and how they shape style, mood, and silhouette.

competencies.description: Creative Thinking and Innovation: Ability to generate original design ideas and apply creativity in clothing construction and decoration
Problem-Solving Skills: Identify and solve design and construction challenges using appropriate tools and techniques
Communication: Express design ideas clearly through sketches, oral presentations, and written descriptions
Collaboration and Teamwork: Work effectively in groups during practical work or design projects
Entrepreneurial Awareness: Develop an understanding of how clothing design can lead to income-generating opportunities
Environmental and Social Responsibility: Recognize sustainable practices in fabric selection and clothing production
Specific Competence 1.7.1.1: Create suitable textile design

sub_topics.name: 1.7.2 Sub-topic: Principle of Design
sub_topics.description: Covers design rules—including balance (symmetrical, asymmetrical, radial), harmony, emphasis, rhythm, proportion, and unity—and their application to fashion and interior design items.

competencies.description: Specific competence 1.7.2.1: Apply different principles of design

sub_topics.name: 1.7.3 Sub-topic: Figure Types
sub_topics.description: Examines distinct human body silhouettes (hourglass, pear, apple, rectangle, inverted triangle), teaching learners how to select and design flattering garment styles while avoiding common fashion mistakes.

competencies.description: Specific Competence 1.7.3.1: Select personal outfits according to figure types

topics.name: TOPIC 1.8: CONSTRUCTION PROCESSES
topics.description: Outlines the practical steps required to turn textile components into finished garments through pattern drafting, stitching, pressing, fitting, and neatening techniques.

sub_topics.name: 1.8.1 Sub-topic: Stitches
sub_topics.description: Covers hand stitching techniques categorized into temporary (basting), permanent (joining, neatening), and decorative stitches for functional garment assembly and aesthetic finishing.

competencies.description: Analytical Thinking: Identify different types of textiles and their sources
Critical Thinking: Understanding fabric properties and how they interact with patterns and sewing techniques
Emotional Intelligence: Practical Work - Hand Stitching Tasks
Problem Solving: Recognize the importance of sustainable practices during sewing
Financial Literacy: Explore Career Opportunities in sewing Industry
Specific Competence: Work out different hand stitches

sub_topics.name: 1.8.2 Sub-topic: Pressing and Ironing
sub_topics.description: Teaches the distinction between pressing and ironing, detailing equipment use, temperature settings, and techniques for pressing seams, darts, and pleats to achieve clean garment lines.

competencies.description: Specific Competence: Press and Iron articles during construction

topics.name: 1.9 TOPIC: GARMENT CONSTRUCTION
topics.description: Garment making is the craft of designing, cutting, and stitching clothing, fulfilling basic needs while enabling cultural expression. It contributes to economic growth, job creation, and innovation in the fashion industry. For learners, it builds creative, technical, and problem-solving skills, promoting self-expression and sustainable practices.

competencies.description: Analytical Thinking - Analyse different fabrics and garment designs to understand their suitability for specific needs and purposes.
Collaboration - Work in teams to design, cut, and sew garments, sharing tasks, resources, and ideas effectively.
Communication - Effectively communicate ideas and garment designs through sketches, verbal explanations, and written descriptions.
Creativity and Innovation - Apply creative thinking to design unique garments or adapt existing designs, using innovative techniques and ideas.
Critical Thinking - Evaluate garment-construction processes and designs critically, identifying areas for improvement or alternatives.
Digital Literacy - Use digital tools to research garment design trends, create digital patterns, and enhance garment-making techniques.
Environmental Sustainability - Practice sustainable garment construction processes by using eco-friendly materials, reducing waste, and promoting ethical production.
Financial Literacy - Manage resources effectively in garment-construction projects, including budgeting for materials and time.
Problem Solving - Apply problem-solving techniques to overcome challenges in garment construction, such as fabric defects or design issues.

sub_topics.name: 1.9.1 Sub-topic: Notions
sub_topics.description: This lesson introduces learners to notions which are; small items or accessories used in garment construction, such as zippers, buttons, threads, elastics, and trims. It highlights the importance of notions in enhancing the functionality, design, and durability of garments.
learning_objectives: Activity 1: Define notions and describe their importance in garment construction.
Activity 2: Describe different types of notions used in fashion and fabric construction.
Activity 3: Explain functions of various notions in garment design and construction.
Activity 4: Using appropriate notions for different garments, sew a button onto fabric, ensuring you create a buttonhole and securely attach the button for both functional and decorative purposes.

competencies.description: 1.9.1.1 Specific Competences: Use notions

sub_topics.name: 1.9.2 Sub-topic: Pattern markings
sub_topics.description: Pattern markings are crucial in garment construction as they serve as guides for cutting, assembling, and sewing garments accurately. Understanding and applying pattern markings ensure precision and efficiency, resulting in professional-quality garments.
learning_objectives: Activities 1: Discussing the importance of pattern markings in garment construction
Activity 2: Demonstrating Methods of Transferring Pattern Markings
Activity 3: Recognizing Methods for Accurate Pattern Markings.
Activity 4: Interpreting symbols used in pattern markings
Activity 5: Applying Pattern markings on fabric altering and adapting patterns to fit different figures.
Activity 6: Practical alteration project.

competencies.description: 1.9.2.1 Specific Competences: Transfer different pattern markings

sub_topics.name: 1.9.3 Sub-topic: Pattern drafting
sub_topics.description: Pattern drafting is a foundational skill in garment making that involves creating templates or patterns that guide the cutting and assembly of fabric into garments.
learning_objectives: Activity 1: Discussing Types of Paper Patterns.
Activity 2: Importance of Pattern Drafting in Garment Making.
Activity 3: Taking Accurate Body Measurements.
Activity 4: Making Basic Patterns Using Measurements.
Activity 5: Modifying Basic Patterns for Different Designs and fits.
Activity 5: Modifying Basic Patterns For Different Designs and fits.

competencies.description: 1.9.3.1 Specific Competences: Draft different patterns

sub_topics.name: 1.9.4 Sub-topic: Seams
sub_topics.description: Seams are the fundamental building blocks of garment construction as they join pieces of fabric together to create a finished product. When choosing the appropriate seam, several factors must be considered such as the type of fabric, the purpose of the garment and the desired appearance.
learning_objectives: Activity 1: Discussing Seams. (definition, factor to consider when choosing seams).
Activity 2: Classifying Seams (conspicuous(visible)-overlaid, run and fell and inconspicuous (invisible) -open and French…)
Activity 3: Working out different Seams. (practical)

competencies.description: 1.9.4.1 Specific Competence: Work out different Seams

sub_topics.name: 1.9.5 Sub-topic: Disposal of fullness
sub_topics.description: In garment construction, disposal of fullness refers to managing excess fabric to ensure a proper fit and achieve the desired design. Fullness is often added to areas like skirts, bodices, or sleeves for comfort or style.
learning_objectives: Activity 1: Discussing disposing of fullness in garments. (definition, Reasons of disposal of fullness…)
Activity 2: Explaining different methods of disposing of fullness (gathers, pleats, tucks, darts…).
Activity 3: Using suitable method on appropriate fabric (pleats- polyester, gathers- cotton…)
Activity 4: Identifying positions where different methods can be used (Gathers- Waistline and armholes, Darts: waistline, Bust, Tucks- armholes…)
Activity 5: Apply different methods of disposal of fullness on garment: (skirts, apron…)

competencies.description: 1.9.5.1 Specific Competences: Apply different methods of reducing fullness of garments

sub_topics.name: 1.9.6 Sub-topic: Pockets
sub_topics.description: Pockets are essential features in garments, adding both functionality and style. They are used to hold personal items and can enhance a garment's design.
learning_objectives: Activity 1: Discussing pockets (definition, uses…)
Activity 2: Classifying pockets (Patch, Inside/Inseam, and Inset)
Activity 3: Discussing uses of pockets (storage, warmth, style, security)
Activity 4: Working out pockets.

competencies.description: 1.9.6.1 Specific Competences: Work out different pockets

sub_topics.name: 1.9.7 Sub-topic: Waistline finishes
sub_topics.description: Waistline finishes are techniques used to finish the waist area of a garment, providing structure, comfort, and durability. These finishes help secure the garment at the waist and prevent fabric fraying.
learning_objectives: Activity 1: Discuss different types of waistlines (empire, high, natural, dropped, hip hug...).
Activity 2: Choosing appropriate fabrics and materials for different types of waistline finishes.
Activity 3: Work out different waistline finishes: (Casing , waistband, Facing…)

competencies.description: 1.9.7.1 Specific Competences: Finish waistline

topics.name: 1.10 TOPIC: CRAFTS
topics.description: Crafts involve creating objects by hand using different materials and techniques. It is a form of artistic expression that can be functional, decorative, or both.

competencies.description: Analytical thinking - Understand the different types of crafts and their history.
Creativity and Innovation - Develop basic skills in specific crafts (e.g., drawing, painting, clay modelling).
Analytical thinking - Identify the tools and materials needed for various crafts.
Critical thinking - Demonstrate safety measures when working with craft tools.
Creativity and Innovation - Create simple craft projects using learned techniques.

sub_topics.name: 1.10.1 Sub-topic: Crocheting
sub_topics.description: Crocheting is a fun craft that involves a few basic tools and techniques. In this lesson you will need a crochet hook, scissors, and safety pins. You will also learn common crochet abbreviations like ss, sc, and dc.
learning_objectives: Activity 1: Identifying tools to be used when crocheting. (crochet hook, scissors, safety pins)
Activity 2: Interpreting crocheting abbreviations. (ss, sc, dc…)
Activity 3: Working out crotchet stitches: (Double, Single).

competencies.description: 1.10.1.1 Specific Competence: Work out crochet stitches

topics.name: 1.11 TOPIC: ENTREPRENEURSHIP
topics.description: Entrepreneurship is the engine of innovation, growth, and change in today’s world. It is the process to develop, organise, and run a new business enterprise by accepting some risks and challenges in order to make profit.

competencies.description: Analytical Thinking - Analyse different small business ventures. Demonstrate understanding of entrepreneurship and entrepreneur.
Communication - Effectively communicate ideas through verbal explanations, and written descriptions.
Creativity and Innovation - Apply creative thinking to design unique garments or adapt existing designs, using innovative techniques and ideas. Discuss Entrepreneurship Skills in Fashion and Fabrics
Digital Literacy - Using digital tools for marketing (social media, content creation…) Running e-commerce platforms or online boutiques
Financial Literacy - Pricing garments or services competitively and managing startup capital and profits. Understanding taxes, investments, and financial risks.
Problem Solving - Apply problem-solving techniques to overcome challenges in entrepreneurship. Finding solutions to maintain creativity while staying within budget.
Empathy and Emotional Intelligence - Analyse the characteristics of an entrepreneur
Critical thinking - Analyse the characteristics of an entrepreneur
Planning and Organization - Make a Simple Business Plan

sub_topics.name: 1.11.1 Sub-topic: Entrepreneurship
sub_topics.description: Entrepreneurship is considered to be the combination of 'entrepreneur' and 'enterprise.' The word 'entrepreneur' is derived from the French verb entrepreneur, which means 'to undertake'. This refers to those who 'undertake' the risk of new enterprises.
learning_objectives: Activity 1: Discussing the concept of entrepreneurship and its importance in the fashion and fabrics industry.
Activity 2: Identifying various business opportunities in the fashion and fabrics sector.
Activity 3: Developing a simple business idea related to fashion and fabrics.
Activity 4: Demonstrating basic principles of managing a small business in the fashion industry.
Activity 5: Writing a brief business plan, and presenting it to the class.

competencies.description: 1.11.1.1 Specific Competence: Apply entrepreneurial skills
